page.description: Guidelines for color usage in med.o products and applications

overview.aboutBody: Color is a fundamental design element that communicates meaning, enhances usability, and helps establish a consistent brand identity. In the med.o design system, colors are carefully chosen to support accessibility, ensure consistency, and reflect the system's visual language.
overview.principlesTitle: Principles of Color Usage in med.o
overview.p1Body: Colors in the med.o design system meet or exceed WCAG 2.1 AA contrast standards. This ensures content remains readable for all users, including those with visual impairments. Always verify color combinations — especially text against backgrounds — to ensure they meet contrast requirements.
overview.p2Body: Use styling hooks consistently when applying custom styles. These hooks help maintain a cohesive look across all med.o products. Avoid hardcoding colors so your design can adapt to different themes.
overview.p3Body: The med.o design system assigns specific colors to represent states such as success, error, or warning. These hooks use semantic naming, making their purpose clear. Use these predefined hooks instead of custom color values.
overview.t1Body: Our color palette is built on clean white surfaces, accented with intentional bursts of vibrant color. These highlights draw attention to key information without overwhelming the interface.
overview.t2Body: Consistent use of styling hooks allows users to quickly associate specific colors with their intended meanings.
overview.t3Body: Thoughtful color choices help direct attention, support navigation, and make it easier for users to complete tasks efficiently.
overview.t4Body: Vibrant color combinations are used sparingly to create moments of visual interest, while keeping information-dense interfaces clear and easy to understand.
overview.foundationalBody: Foundational colors give meaning to specific UI elements. Use them only for their intended purpose so users can consistently associate a color with the same meaning throughout the product.
overview.fl1Body: Full spectrum of colors without fixed assignment — usable for undefined situations.
overview.fl2Body: Colors with no semantic assignment, but commonly used by semantic hooks for UI elements.
overview.fl3Body: Used for building components and UI page elements such as backgrounds, borders, and fills. Use these colors only for their respective locations.
overview.mappedColorsLink: Learn more about mapped colors in the Tokens tab.

usage.title: When to Use Which Color
usage.intro: Always use semantic UI tokens instead of raw brand color values. This ensures future theme changes adapt automatically.
usage.semanticBody: Semantic tokens like --color-text-primary or --color-success describe intent, not the actual color value. They are the preferred choice for all UI components, as they automatically support theme changes.
usage.rawBody: Brand tokens like --color-brand-navy-500 or --color-brand-orange-800 are appropriate for themed areas and brand assets — or when no semantic equivalent exists.
usage.dontNote: Use raw tokens or hex values
usage.statesBody: Every interactive color group follows a defined state sequence: Default → Hover → Active → Disabled. Always use the corresponding token pairs — never manually calculate lighter or darker variants.
usage.surfaceBody: The system defines two primary surface levels. Level 1 is the default page background, Level 2 is the subtly elevated area. For cards and containers within these levels, use the Surface Container tokens.
usage.a11yBody: Text on colored backgrounds must meet WCAG 2.1 AA: minimum 4.5:1 contrast for normal text, 3:1 for large text (18 px+ or 14 px bold). Use --color-text-on-color on --surface_inverse or --surface_brand backgrounds.
usage.themeBody: The design system is designed for future dark mode support. Semantic tokens are the only theme-aware layer. Use only semantic tokens in component code — never direct brand or alias values.

page.description: Type system and typography guidelines for med.o products and applications

overview.scaleBody: The med.o type system covers 10 sizes — from 12 px (xs) to 60 px (6xl). Each size maps to a semantic use case: Display for hero areas, Headings for structural hierarchy, Body for reading content, and Labels for small UI elements.
overview.sansBody: DM Sans — primary sans-serif for all UI text, labels, and headings.
overview.monoBody: DM Mono — monospace for code, tokens, and technical identifiers.
overview.contextBody: Here is how type levels look in a typical page section: a Label SM marks the category, Heading XL forms the page title, Body LG provides the descriptive introduction, and Body MD carries the main content.

usage.title: Typography Guidelines
usage.intro: Always use the defined typography tokens. Hardcoded pixel values in CSS or JSX are not allowed — they break consistency and make system-wide changes difficult.
usage.headingBody: The system defines six heading levels: Display 2XL and Display XL for large hero areas, Heading XL through Heading SM for page structure. Always use the next-higher level as the parent — do not skip hierarchy levels.
usage.headingH1: H1 / Display 2XL — Page title, used once per page. Not for sub-sections.
usage.headingH2: H2 / Heading XL or LG — Primary sections of a page.
usage.headingH3: H3 / Heading MD or SM — Sub-sections, card titles, panel headings.
usage.headingH4: H4 and below — Only for densely structured content (documentation, tables).
usage.bodyBody: Body LG (18 px / 1.65) is suited for extended reading content. Body MD (16 px / 1.5) is the default for UI text and descriptions. Body SM (14 px) for help text and metadata.
usage.labelBody: Label MD (14 px / 500) for interactive elements like buttons and form fields. Label SM (12 px / 600 / Caps) for categorizing labels in tables, tags, and badges.
usage.codeBody: For inline code and code blocks, always use --font-mono (DM Mono). Combine with --text-sm and --leading-relaxed for optimal readability.
usage.lineLengthBody: Optimal line length for body text: 60–80 characters on desktop, 45–60 on mobile. Lines that are too short interrupt reading flow; lines that are too long cause eye fatigue. Use max-w-[65ch] or max-w-prose as a reference value.
usage.formattingBody: Write headings in sentence case (capitalize first letter only). Use bold sparingly — only for genuine emphasis with [font-weight:var(--weight-semibold)]. Label SM is always uppercase (text-transform: uppercase) with --tracking-widest.
